reviews.title: Needs more levels!
reviews.text:
I played every level, and I keep thinking that they will add more levels. But it’s been over a year and nothing has changed. 
I really liked this game, it’s like a cup of hot tea on a cold day- so relaxing. My only complaint is not enough levels. The ads didn’t go away when I paid for the “no ads” option”, so don’t waste money on that.  Just turn on the airplane mode and all the ads go away. I don’t usually like to turn on the airplane mode, I like to have options, but when they charge a price higher than my weekly gas bill- I’m out.

reviews.text: I love this game. I’ve played it for over a year and I’m dying for a new update. It’s the best kind of repetition with new and increasingly harder levels.

reviews.title: Over priced
reviews.text: Graphics are ok for a phone game but the price for not having to watch adds is ridiculous. And on top of that, the frequency at which you have to watch adds if you don’t pay is insulting.

reviews.title: Good game, but has its limits
reviews.text: Before you get too into the game, because it is very addicting, know that it currently only has 18 levels. I was sick this weekend and was pretty much stuck on the couch, and went through all 18 levels in about 4-5 days. Had I known there were only 18 levels, I honestly would have chosen a different game to invest my time and money in.

reviews.title: In-app purchases don’t work
reviews.text: Was being impatient and threw 3.99 at a 25 pack of bombs. It said success, but no bombs. I set my banking app up to text me any time I am charged for anything, so I got the notification and knew I had been charged. So I restarted my game, checked if there was a mail system it could be caught in…nothing. I double checked bank at that point, logging in to confirm I wasn’t mistaken and had been charged. The charge was definitely there.

reviews.title: Super cash grab rip
reviews.text: Buying no ads costs more than some of the higher quality games found on Steam. I don’t get why developers have adopted this almost mafia style ad tactic on mobile apps instead of just developing something that doesn’t drive people away. I instantly delete more games by a long shot than I even play longer than 5 minutes.

reviews.title: Paying for no ads, gets you less ads.
reviews.text:
When you purchase the No ads options, that doesn’t mean you will never get ads again. Only the automated ad breaks. I really enjoyed this game enough to purchase the $20 ad free option.  But, I am still getting ads. 
It’s like ordering a hamburger specifically without mayo and still getting a thin layer of mayo on it. What!?
